title: Retrieval-Augmented Fine-Tuning for Improving Retrieve-and-Edit Based Assertion Generation
year_venue: 2025 IEEE Transactions on Software Engineering, vol. 51 no. 5 (primary PDF), DOI 10.1109/TSE.2025.3558403
datasets: Dataatlas (156,760 TAP items overall; 15,676 test examples) and Dataintegration (265,420 items overall; 26,542 test examples), random 8:1:1 splits not project-disjoint; same projects may occur in train and test.
New cross-project test set of 15,676 Methods2Test TAPs, projects filtered to avoid train-project overlap.
Defects4J 2.0.0: paper states 835 bugs in 17 projects; focuses on 588 assertion-triggerable bugs; excludes exception-testing prefixes from assertion-generation evaluation.
models: Main CodeT5-base 223M; paper also directly evaluates Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct with CoT on assertion inference.
artifact_url: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.15118614 (paper-linked replication package); https://github.com/Lhy-apple/EditAs2 (matching public source repo).
license: Zenodo record CC BY 4.0; GitHub source archive has no explicit root software license
input_setting: Input is a test prefix without assertions plus focal method; retrieval uses a training TAP as prototype. Defects4J evaluation combines generated assertion with EvoSuite-generated prefixes (from buggy versions) or supplied bug-triggering test prefixes, then checks failure on buggy and pass on fixed program. Not issue-report input or root-cause diagnosis.
reproduction_grade: B- (public source/data/model archive route; exact replay conditional on 1.94GB package inspection, env/path repair, immutable weights and weak precision)
concept_hook: High: retrieval exemplar + focal-test semantic-edit representation for assertions; exact Qwen2.5-Coder-7B-Instruct baseline aligns with project, but no Qwen Defects4J bug-found metric.
limitation: Dataset train/test split is not project-disjoint; compilation 30.97%, precision 0.42%; source archive uses old dependencies/hard-coded paths.
